escena: SCENE (two stages of one piece, studio in Miami, evening, NO recognisable faces): A TRUE IN-CAMERA DOUBLE EXPOSURE — two moments of the same work occupy the same frame at once, and BOTH are visible THROUGH each other, neither one covering the other. Verify it by these landmarks: the first exposure is a rough pencil sketch on paper, its lines dark and legible; the second exposure is the finished piece glowing AZURE BLUE, and the two are SUPERIMPOSED so the blue of the finished version shows THROUGH the paper of the sketch and the pencil lines run ACROSS the finished artwork; where the two overlap the image is brighter, because light was added twice. The bright areas of one exposure fill the dark areas of the other. This is a real double exposure made on one frame, NOT a collage, NOT two images side by side and NOT a transparent layer pasted on top: there is no hard edge anywhere between them. A single ORANGE grease pencil lies in the sketch exposure, the only warm colour. 50mm at f/4. Everything is completely unbranded, no readable text anywhere.
